manifest_words.finding: The v1.7 manifest 'words' did NOT match the canonical HTML under the spec rule (L441: <main> minus .abstract/.claim-strip/.vps-aside/h1/nav). Residuals were page-specific and BIDIRECTIONAL — on most pages the manifest was lower than the HTML count (by up to 5.3% on 01), but on 07 it was higher (by 1.0%). A single tokenizer applied to fixed text cannot produce counts that are lower than the HTML reference on seven pages and higher on the eighth; that split rules out a pure tokenizer mismatch and points to the numbers having been generated at an earlier content state (or from source documents) — i.e. STALE. This matches the v1.7 gate's own note that counts were 'pending author reconcile_derived_to_html.py'.
manifest_words.action: Per Constitution C1 the canonical HTML is the SSOT and derived counts are recomputed from it. The reconcile step (reconcile_manifest_words in upgrade_chemistry_v1_8.py) rewrote 'words' = body_words(HTML) for all 8 pages, using a tokenizer byte-identical to gate_v1_8.py:body_words. The manifest now equals the HTML count exactly (gate manifest_words_within_0.5pct PASS, 0% difference).
manifest_words.note: This resolves the earlier 'author must reconcile later' item for the chemistry paper. If the author's own inventory.py uses a different tokenizer, any per-page disagreement >0.5% would surface in their gate; the exclusion set here follows spec L441 exactly.

body_invariance.word_count_effect: The retag moves the two heading texts from the h1-excluded zone into the counted body: 01 gains 9 words, 06 gains 10 words (exactly the heading words); the other 6 pages are unchanged. Measured with one consistent tokenizer.

inherited_defects.severity: FAIL inherited (pre-existing in v1.7 source) -> REPAIRED this phase
inherited_defects.detail: Each page tagged one appended SECTION heading as <h1> instead of <h2>, violating 'exactly one h1'. The mis-tagged headings are peers of the page's other id-bearing section headings (all <h2>); the page title is the only <h1> and carries no id. The v1.7 gate reported new_h1_one:PASS in error; this report corrects that record.
inherited_defects.resolution: Retagged each mis-tagged <h1 id=...> to <h2> (matched by exact id, so the title h1 is never touched). After fix every page (and the hub) has exactly one h1 — verified by new gate check h1_exactly_one (9 docs, 0 violations). No heading text was altered.
inherited_defects.manifest_reconciliation: The retag moves each heading text from the h1-excluded zone into the counted body (+9 on 01, +10 on 06). Rather than leave this for later, the manifest 'words' was fully reconciled to the canonical HTML this phase (see manifest_words) — so 01/06 already reflect the retag and every page now matches the HTML within the spec's 0.5% rule. No outstanding word-count action remains.

inherited_defects.detail: The v1.7 hub CollectionPage hasPart listed only 7 of 8 chapters (07-low-grade-waste-heat-electricity missing) — the structured-data twin of the merged 6/7 <li> TOC defect.
inherited_defects.resolution: Repaired in-lane (JSON-LD is an allowed edit surface): during the CollectionPage->Book conversion, the script inserts the missing ch.07 entry before ax-o, preserving every original headline verbatim (SSOT = _meta chapter order). The hub hasPart is now 8 entries. The merged 6/7 <li> in the visible TOC was also split into two correct items.

judgment_calls: The Phase-0 kit (tools/, templates/) is absent from the handoff. Under a strict reading of spec section 13 this would read as 'Phase 0 kit missing'. Chosen response: a faithful ADDITIVE deterministic upgrade via a self-written, hash-pinned script that honors 'code is the agent', minimal edit surfaces, and reproducibility — rather than refusing. The author should fold this script (or its equivalent) into the official tools/ lane.

Two mis-tagged section headings were retagged from <h1> to <h2> (an inherited defect; see inherited_defects: multiple-h1). This is one structural edit beyond the v1.8 answer/JSON-LD surfaces, taken under explicit owner delegation because it is an unambiguous spec-conformance fix (the sibling section headings are all <h2>) and leaves all body text byte-identical. The resulting +9/+10 word shift into the counted body is accounted for by the full manifest reconciliation performed this phase (see manifest_words).

_meta.json grade enum is documented as forced|calibrated|open|null, but the spec's grade-badge rule yields hypothesis (S5) and verified (S7) from body token frequency. The script writes the TRUE computed grade; the _meta enum should be widened to include hypothesis|verified, or the rule clarified.
